name: XypherSEO
author: Mansi Bhardwaj

sections.description:
XypherSEO is a full SEO plugin for WordPress. It puts a search optimization workspace directly below your post editor, scores the page while you write it, shows you exactly how the result will look in Google and on social platforms, and gives you the site-wide tools most sites end up installing three separate plugins for.

Everything described below is included. There is no account to create, no API key to paste, no usage cap, and no feature that stops working after a trial period. The plugin does not phone home. Every check runs on your own server against your own content.

Score every page while you write it

The editor panel runs 30 individual on-page checks and turns them into a single score out of 100, grouped into four levels so you always know what to fix next.

  • Live scoring. The score updates as you type. No save, no reload, no separate analyze button to remember.
  • Grouped checklist. Checks are split into Basics, Intermediate, Advanced and Pro, so a new writer sees the handful of things that matter and an experienced one sees all thirty.
  • A specific fix for every failed check. Not “improve readability” but the actual change to make on this page.
  • Word count and keyword count, shown live, including on pages built with Elementor and other page builders.

The checks cover focus keyword placement in the title, slug, opening paragraph, subheadings and image alt text; title and meta description length against what Google actually displays; keyword density; internal and outbound linking; sentence and paragraph readability; subheading distribution; keyword variations; and whether the page uses a list or table.

See the result before you publish

  • Google SERP preview with separate desktop and mobile rendering, updating as you type, showing the favicon, site name, URL, title and description as they will appear.
  • Character counters on the SEO title and meta description with the recommended range marked, so you stop guessing where Google truncates.
  • Social previews for four platforms: Facebook, X, LinkedIn and Pinterest, each rendered separately.
  • Per-platform overrides. Facebook and X titles and descriptions inherit from your SEO fields automatically, and you can override any of them individually. Custom Open Graph image supported, with the featured image used as the fallback.

Structured data you control

  • JSON-LD fields for FAQPage, HowTo and Product, plus a free-form field for any other schema type you need.
  • Article and BreadcrumbList structured data generated automatically from your content.
  • Everything you paste is validated as JSON before it saves, so broken markup never reaches a live page.
  • A structured data report showing what is present on the page and what is missing.

Site-wide tools

  • XML sitemaps. A sitemap index at /xypher-sitemap.xml with separate sitemaps for posts, pages, custom post types, taxonomies and authors. Styled with an XSL stylesheet so it is readable when opened in a browser rather than a wall of raw XML.
  • Redirect manager. 301, 302, 307 and 308 redirects, with regular expression support and a per-rule hit counter so you can see which redirects are actually being used.
  • 404 monitor. Logs every missing URL visitors hit, so you can find and redirect the ones that matter instead of guessing.
  • Breadcrumbs with BreadcrumbList structured data, output anywhere with the [xypher_breadcrumbs] shortcode.
  • Conflict detection. Warns you when another SEO plugin is writing duplicate meta tags or a competing sitemap, rather than letting you silently ship two of everything.
  • Canonical and robots controls per page: noindex, nofollow, noarchive, nosnippet and noimageindex.
  • Import and export of your settings and redirects as CSV.
  • Safe mode. One switch that stops all front-end output while leaving the admin screens working, so you can rule the plugin in or out when diagnosing a theme or caching problem.
  • Setup wizard on first activation. Pick which content types show the SEO panel and whether to generate a sitemap.

Free, and staying free

This plugin is complete. Everything above is included for every user with no restrictions, no credits and no expiry.

Two paid plugins with a broader feature set are available separately at xypherseo.com. They are optional. Nothing in this plugin depends on them, prompts you to buy them, or stops working without them.

Privacy

XypherSEO stores its data in your WordPress database and sends nothing anywhere. There is no external service, no telemetry, no tracking and no third-party API. Deleting the plugin removes everything it created.
sections.installation:
Installing from your dashboard

  1. In WordPress admin, go to Plugins > Add New.
  2. Search for XypherSEO.
  3. Click Install Now, then Activate.

Installing a zip file

  1. Download the plugin zip.
  2. Go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  3. Choose the zip file, click Install Now, then Activate.

Installing over FTP

  1. Unzip the plugin.
  2. Upload the xypherseo folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  3. Activate it from the Plugins screen.

First run

Activation opens a short setup wizard once. It asks two things:

  1. Which content types show the SEO panel. Posts and pages by default. Add any custom post types you optimize.
  2. Whether to generate an XML sitemap. Enable this unless another plugin is already handling your sitemap.

Click Save and finish. That is the whole setup.

Where everything lives

All site-wide tools sit under the XypherSEO menu in the admin sidebar:

  • Settings. Content types, sitemap options, breadcrumbs, safe mode, CSV import and export.
  • Sitemaps. Choose which post types, taxonomies and authors are included, and view the generated sitemap.
  • Redirects. Add, edit and delete redirect rules. Each rule shows its hit count.
  • 404 Monitor. Every missing URL visitors have hit, with a count and the last time it happened.

Per-page controls are in the XypherSEO panel below the editor on any post or page, organised into tabs for the analysis, social previews, schema and advanced settings.

Getting your first page scored

  1. Open any post or page.
  2. Scroll to the XypherSEO panel below the editor.
  3. Enter a focus keyword, the phrase you want this page to rank for.
  4. The score and checklist populate immediately and update as you edit.
  5. Work down the checklist. Each failed item tells you the specific change to make.

Bundled assets

This plugin bundles the Poppins typeface for the admin interface. Poppins is licensed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1, which is GPL compatible. The full license text is included at admin/fonts/LICENSE.txt.
sections.faq:
Is XypherSEO really free?

Yes. Every feature described on this page is in the free plugin, available to every user, with no account, no credits, no usage limits and no trial period. It is GPL licensed and it stays free.

Two paid plugins with a broader feature set are sold separately at xypherseo.com. They are entirely optional and separate. This plugin does not check for a license, does not nag you to upgrade, and does not withhold anything from you.

Where do I buy the paid plugins?

At xypherseo.com. They are separate downloads and are not part of this plugin.

Does this plugin require an account, an API key or an external service?

No. There is nothing to sign up for and nothing to connect. Every check runs on your own server against your own content. The plugin makes no outbound requests and transmits no data anywhere.

Does XypherSEO replace Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress or All in One SEO?

Yes. It is a full replacement, not an add-on. It handles titles, meta descriptions, canonicals, robots directives, Open Graph and Twitter Card tags, structured data, XML sitemaps, breadcrumbs, redirects and 404 monitoring.

You should not run it alongside another SEO plugin. Two SEO plugins will each write their own meta tags and sitemaps, and search engines will see duplicates. XypherSEO detects this and warns you, but the fix is to pick one and deactivate the other.

Will it conflict with my existing schema markup?

If another SEO plugin is active, yes, you will get duplicate structured data. That is true of any two SEO plugins, not just this one. The built-in conflict check tells you when it is happening.

If XypherSEO is your only SEO plugin, there is no conflict. Article and BreadcrumbList schema are generated automatically, and anything you add manually in the Schema tab is validated as JSON before it saves, so malformed markup never reaches a live page.

Will it slow my site down?

No. All analysis happens in the admin while you are editing, never on the front end. On the front end the plugin outputs meta tags and JSON-LD, which is a handful of lines in the page head. Sitemaps are generated on request, not on every page load.

How do I add FAQ structured data?

Open the Schema tab in the XypherSEO panel below the editor, paste valid FAQPage JSON-LD into the FAQ field, and update the post. It is checked as valid JSON when you save and output in the page head. There are separate fields for HowTo and Product schema, and a free-form field for any other type.

Where is my XML sitemap?

At /xypher-sitemap.xml on your site once you enable it. That is a sitemap index that links to separate sitemaps for posts, pages, custom post types, taxonomies and authors. It is styled so it is readable when you open it in a browser.

WordPress ships its own core sitemap. XypherSEO replaces it when you turn the XypherSEO sitemap on.

How do I redirect a broken URL?

Go to XypherSEO > 404 Monitor to see which URLs visitors are actually hitting. Then go to XypherSEO > Redirects, add a rule with the old URL as the source and the new one as the destination, and pick the status code. Use 301 for a permanent move, which is what you want in almost every case. Each rule tracks how many times it has fired.

Does it work with Elementor and other page builders?

Yes. Content analysis reads the rendered content, so word count, keyword count and every content-based check work correctly on pages built with Elementor and similar builders, rather than reporting zero.

What does safe mode do?

It stops the plugin writing anything to the front end: no meta tags, no structured data, no Open Graph tags, no breadcrumbs. The admin screens keep working normally.

It exists so you can determine whether a display problem is caused by this plugin without deactivating it and losing your settings. Turn it on, check the page, turn it off.

What are the four levels in the checklist?

The 30 checks are grouped by how much they matter and how much work they take. Basics covers the fundamentals every page needs. Intermediate covers title structure, content length and linking. Advanced covers readability and content depth. Pro covers the refinements that separate a good page from a well-optimized one.

Clear Basics on every page first, then work down as you have time. All thirty checks are available to every user.

Can I move my settings between sites?

Yes. XypherSEO > Settings has CSV import and export for your settings and your redirect rules, so you can set up one site and replicate it, or keep a backup before making changes.

Will my data be removed if I delete the plugin?

Yes. Deleting XypherSEO through the Plugins screen removes its options, its post meta and its database tables. Deactivating it leaves everything in place, so you can deactivate safely while troubleshooting.

Is this white-hat SEO?

Yes. Every check is based on published guidance from search engines about on-page quality: clear titles, accurate descriptions, sensible heading structure, readable content, descriptive alt text and valid structured data. There is nothing here that manipulates rankings or that you would need to hide.
sections.changelog:
1.9.9

  • Rebuilt as a single, fully functional plugin. Every feature is available to every user, with no restrictions.
  • Structured data is entered manually as JSON-LD and validated on save.
  • On-page scoring with a grouped checklist and a specific fix for each failed check.
  • Sitemap stylesheet moved to a separate CSS file.
  • Text domain corrected to match the plugin slug.
  • Added an uninstall routine that removes all plugin data.

1.8.9

  • Earlier release.
